messages.subject: construct a bayesian graph
parts: Hi all, I'm very new to machine learning. I have some questions that may be very trivial for some of you. In fact, I have data and I wish to use them to learn the structure of the graph as well as to learn the parameter of a bayesian graph, then do some inference. At first, I installed free version of R and Rstan in order to achieve this job. However I don't know from where to start. I have read about IP and PC algorithms that enable to construct a bayesian graph using conditional independence tests. I have some idea how to simplify these algorithms to accord to my simple model. However, can some one provide some basic informations how to use Rstan and R in my case. I don't know from where I start. thanks.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] construct a bayesian graph
parts:
https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/wiki/RStan-Getting-Started

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/rstan/

http://mc-stan.org/documentation/

You may find learning graph structure beyond what Stan can do
given that it's a discrete problem.

- Bob
